label: XGS-PON OLT class N1, 16 ports
notes: ITU-T G.9807.1 (02/2023), basic wavelength set. Table B.9.2: class N1 is an ODN attenuation range of 14-29 dB. Table B.9.3 (9.95328 Gbit/s downstream): OLT mean launched power +2.0..+5.0 dBm; the ONU receiver is -28.0 dBm sensitivity and -9.0 dBm overload for every class, which is what the XGS-PON ONT row carries. Table B.9.4 (9.95328 Gbit/s upstream): OLT receiver sensitivity -26.0 dBm, minimum overload -5.0 dBm; ONU mean launch +4.0..+9.0 dBm. The two directions land 1 dB above their receiver at the class limit: 2.0 - 29 = -27.0 dBm at a -28.0 dBm ONT, and 4.0 - 29 = -25.0 dBm at a -26.0 dBm OLT. The 14 dB floor is the other edge: at the +5.0 dBm launch ceiling a 14 dB ODN arrives at exactly the ONT's -9.0 dBm overload, so a shorter span needs a pad, not a longer cable run - the budget's attenuator verdict is the check. Table B.9.2 and Table B.9.3 publish four ODN classes and one ONU receiver: N1 14-29, N2 16-31, E1 18-33 and E2 20-35 dB of ODN loss, all served by an ONU at -28.0 dBm sensitivity and -9.0 dBm overload. There is no N2a/N2b or E2a/E2b ONU in this recommendation: the N2b and E2b strings in the companion ODN-OPL-class code list (000 N1, 001 N2/N2a, 010 N2b, 011 E1, 100 E2/E2a/D, 101 E2b, 110 B+, 111 C+) are PLOAM registration codes inherited from G.987.1, not a second receiver type. The -21.5 dBm sensitivity / -3.5 dBm overload ONU is XG-PON's reduced-budget type (G.987.2 Amd. 1, Table 9-3), a different PON at 2.488 Gbit/s upstream, and the engine refuses an xg-pon ONT on this card by name rather than budget a pairing nobody can build. Corrected 2026-11-27: this note used to say the 2023 edition split N2 and E2 on the ONU side and carried the -21.5 dBm figure - that is G.987.2's table quoted against G.9807.1's. maxSplitRatio 128 is the widely deployed XGS-PON ratio but an operator and line-card option, not a PMD figure - confirm the card's own limit before designing a 1:128 site. Reach is a loss question here: the class's 29 dB bounds the run, and G.9807.1 clauses B.9.2 require support of 20 km (DD20) or 40 km (DD40) with dispersion of 400/800 ps/nm. Wavelengths are 1575-1580 nm downstream and 1260-1280 nm upstream; the engine budgets one wavelength and its PON defaults are 1490 down / 1310 up, whose cable attenuation (0.22 / 0.35 dB/km) sits within 0.01-0.02 dB/km of the real windows. ports 16 is a line-card size, not a standards figure. Class figures from the recommendation, not one measured card: replace the row with the line card actually purchased before construction.
